about.title: Redwood City Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Redwood City recorded one traffic death in 2025, alongside 305 injury collisions and 412 people hurt on its streets. A single number can hide an entire family. When a loved one dies because someone else was careless — on US-101, along Woodside Road, at a crossing on El Camino Real, or in a Middlefield Road neighborhood — California law gives certain survivors the right to bring a civil claim. That claim stands apart from any criminal case the San Mateo County District Attorney may pursue, and it moves on its own timeline. Generally, a spouse or domestic partner and children hold that right first, with certain dependents and heirs able to step in when none survive. The deadline is two years from the date of death, and it shrinks considerably when a public agency is involved. We listen to what happened and handle wrongful death cases on a contingency basis. There is no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Redwood City Families Choose Us

items.title: We help you sort out who can file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to spouses or domestic partners and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. We can explain where your family stands before any paperwork begins.

items.title: We respect the two-year clock
items.desc: A wrongful death claim in California must generally be filed within two years of the date of death, and far sooner if a city, county, or Caltrans is involved. Getting started early keeps those options open.

items.title: The full picture of your loss matters
items.desc: Recoverable losses reach beyond funeral and burial costs to the financial support your loved one provided and the love, companionship, and guidance your family lost. We handle these cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: The driver who caused the crash on Woodside Road is being prosecuted. Do we still need a civil claim?
items.answer: Yes, the two proceed separately. The criminal case belongs to the San Mateo County District Attorney and focuses on punishment, not on compensating your family. A wrongful death claim is a civil action you control, and its two-year deadline keeps running regardless of what happens in criminal court.

items.question: My sibling died and had no spouse or children. Can I bring the claim?
items.answer: Possibly. California gives standing first to a spouse or domestic partner and children, but when none survive, certain dependents and heirs may qualify. We can review your family situation and tell you honestly whether you have the right to file.

items.question: What does it cost to work with us?
items.answer: Nothing at all. We provide free case reviews, and we work on contingency, which means no attorney fee is owed unless there is a recovery in your case.
